claims.claim: XNU exposes memorystatus_level as the integer percentage of its available-page estimate; this advisory allocation headroom is separate from donated resident-page accounting
XNU's pressure sysctl returns dispatch pressure flags; iOS may deny this query, in which case asynchronous pressure and conservative fallback sampling remain active
The macOS-only kernel probe binds registered Mach send rights explicitly when spawning a fresh donor process, using XNU's registered-port spawn attribute
NSXPCCoder provides typed custom encoding and decoding of XPC objects over NSXPCConnection
NSXPCListenerEndpoint can name an anonymous listener across an existing connection
Mach send rights are boxed rather than transferring a task-local numeric port name
Chromium production precedent for an NSSecureCoding object carrying a Mach send right through NSXPCCoder
Runtime-discovered private launch overload passes listenerEndpoint outside generic extension items
Runtime-discovered NSExtensionContext exposes its own auxiliary NSXPCConnection
os_proc_available_memory is advisory current process-limit headroom, not physical device RAM, and its value must not be cached as available capacity
XNU VM statistics include speculative pages in free_count, so speculative pages must not be added again
LiveContainer configures one extension with com.apple.ar.viewer, NSExtensionContext host and guest contexts, and top-level XPCService Application/_MultipleInstances/App metadata
LiveContainer creates an NSExtension request for each guest scene and obtains its PID from the request identifier

limitations: The NSExtension selector and auxiliary connection are private runtime APIs, feature-probed and fail closed.
The extension point and XPCService multiple-instance metadata are private runtime configuration; NeoSwap requires distinct verified donor PIDs and does not infer process isolation from these keys.
The macOS NSXPC service probe does not validate extension suspension, jetsam, signing, or accounting on a physical iPhone.
No app group, ownership-transfer entitlement, global decoder hook, file-backed allocation, or virtual address reservation is used as evidence of donation.
Prepared capacity is distinct from measured resident and compressed memory in the donor kernel ledgers.
Eight independently verified donor PIDs share the same physical device RAM; the aggregate 8 GiB target is never reported as acquired memory.
Each growth chunk is faulted with varying page data and requires its own bidirectional pattern plus incremental and cumulative nonvolatile kernel ledger evidence.
Growth is driven by one host scheduler, bounded by measured process and system headroom, and stops without invalidating previously borrowed chunks when resources are refused.
Resident ledger pages and compressed ledger equivalents are reported separately; compressed equivalents are not physical compressor bytes.
